newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Thousands of Bangladeshi homeless demand shelter.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Bangladeshi homeless demand shelter.

text.p: Thousands of homeless staged a noisy protest in the Bangladesh capital on Wednesday, calling for shelter, burial land and respect for their human rights.
Witnesses said some 5,000 protesters, calling themselves "floating people", gathered outside the national press club in Dhaka and criticised successive governments for neglecting them.
"We don't have a secure place to live, we don't have any safety against predatory musclemen and other repressions," said protest leader Nehar Parveen Runu.

"Shanties we sleep in do not have light or water and are mostly unfit for human living. The worst of all is that the floating population even do not have a place in this city to bury their dead," she said.
Dhaka, one of the world's largest cities, has a current population of more than nine million, and police estimate roughly a quarter of them are homeless.
"And half of the floating people live in the open, on sidewalks, at railway stations and ferry terminals," one police officer said.
The protesters, mostly women sporting red headbands, demanded the government immediately provide safe shelters, develop unused land for a graveyard and give them guarantees against eviction.
"We did not come to the city all very willingly," said Abdus Salam, president of the Floating Workers' Union.
"We were forced to leave villages by lack of work, loss of land either to money lenders or rivers that swallowed our homes."
Police say a large number of the homeless women end up in prostitution.
